title: A Composition Design Strategy for Refractory High-Entropy Alloys.

recollection.intervention: High-entropy alloy design strategy using computational and experimental methods
recollection.structure: Multi-principal element alloys with a single-phase or multi-phase microstructure
recollection.mechanism: Optimization of elemental composition to balance phase stability, mechanical properties, and thermal resistance
recollection.results: Improved mechanical strength and thermal stability in the designed alloys compared to traditional alloys

score.note: The recollection gives only a generic computational/experimental composition-design strategy, without the 38,326-composition screening, VEC/modulus criteria, or selected Nb15Mo2.5Ta40V40W2.5 composition. It does not identify the actual single-phase BCC dendritic structure. The proposed VEC–Peierls barrier–dislocation mobility mechanism is absent, and thermal resistance is unsupported. No quantitative results are recalled; the actual strength change was nuanced, while fracture strain increased from about 2% to 35.7%.
